speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Today, I am going to state I am an aerospace engineer.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I actually work on the Super-Skyhawk A-4SU on Data Bus networking.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But I am also a Fellow at the Royal Aeronautical Society.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: My topic today is on drone but actually, more than drones – the bigger drone or what we call the electric vertical-take-off and landing (eVTOL).

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Common people will say that it is a flying car, air taxis.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Those are interesting stuff that make kids every excited, including adults, I think so.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: For this Motion, I will explore this emerging and high-growth market, dissect the opportunities and challenges that we face in Singapore and propose some strategies and also what initiatives that we can have into building an eVTOL industry going forward.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The first factor is the emerging high-growth market.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: There are two terminologies that we need to be very clear here.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: It is the western perspective and the eastern perspective.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The western perspective calls it "advanced air mobility".

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: It is defined by National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) five years back.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The eastern perspective is we call it the "low-altitude economy", or in Chinese, "低空经济".

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I actually find that the low-altitude economy is more encompassing and that is why I use the terminology low-altitude economy.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The drones that we see in Singapore and regulated by the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) for Unmanned Aircraft Pilot Licence or Drone Pilot Licence up to 25 kilogramme (kg) is Category A and above that is Category B.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We do not have a lot of huge drones in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Mostly, our drone pilots are actually Category A.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, advanced air mobility does not have a lot of presence in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Let us talk about how this low-altitude economy is important for Singapore.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Just imagine that whatever is on the road, whether it is buses, cars, vans, trucks or bicycles, we lift it up like maybe 50 metres, 100 metres into the sky.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Then, we have a completely different set of economy – and that is low-altitude economy.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, the definition of low-altitude economy, up to what height, actually, nobody knows.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I used to have a private pilot licence.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I can fly up to 10,000 feet in Singapore, but maybe we should not fly that high.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But I think 1,000 feet or 300 metres is really good enough.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: It covers the top of all the buildings.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: This can generate new innovations – and I will explain it later – have higher or greater productivity and completely destructive business model.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Let us take a look the market itself.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: If you look at the figures from different research agencies, they are all completely different: some will say $200 billion, some will say $100 billion.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, should we tap on this opportunity to develop a new innovation system, create better jobs and that is highly tech intensive?

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: President Trump last year noted that the United States (US) has to catch up in the advanced air mobility and therefore, there was an executive order signed for the Department of Transportation and Federal Aviation Administration to foster innovations.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, 36 states have already started to implement, whether it is between the airport or within the states.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The other player is really aggressive – China.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Two years ago, I went to the Suzhou Industrial Park with Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Someone handed me a name card, and the title is, Director of Low-Altitude Economy, Suzhou Industrial Park.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: And now, what we have seen is that there are 30 provinces in China actively rolling out low-altitude economy solutions.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I visited a couple of them in different provinces.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I heard that in Guangzhou, there are already 15,000 low-altitude economy companies – dealing with parts, not really the full craft, but you can see the size.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, we can see how big the market is.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The question is: what are the opportunities and challenges that Singapore can work on?

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I do not know whether this number is valid, but I think it warrants some research to see how big this economy is.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Yes, within Singapore, but it is going to be difficult and the safety factor is one of the most important part.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But actually, we can look at the air mobility business, that is, bringing people from one place to another on a regional side – Singapore and Johor, Singapore and Batam, a regional pathway that we can hop from one place to another.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Singapore prides itself, as we do not have domestic destinations for aircraft, but we are international from day one.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, from the view of the low-altitude economy, we should be regional from day one.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, that is air mobility business, air tourism business.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We do not have a lot of land.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But actually, we do have interesting stuff that we can explore within Singapore.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Typical areas for air tourism is like a bird's eye view of the Marina Bay and Sentosa.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I was thinking that even the ports will be interesting to tourists too, with all the container ships floating.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I also think that Mandai Zoo will be a great destination for us to look from the top.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But when I was flying, with my Private Pilot Licence, one time, I did fly a little bit lower to visit the zoo without paying tickets.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The other thing I think that is really important is air logistics, and cross-border logistics is really interesting.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: There are a lot of disruptive business models we can work on, and I will elaborate on this.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Well, highly urbanised space, very good integrated logistics.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, we do not really need to do most of this stuff or in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Our island is slightly more than 700 square kilometres.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: And for us actually to develop or test such a craft, I give you a recent example.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: In the Airshow, the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) unveiled the design of an eVTOL that has done its initial hover test in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But beyond that, the trials had to be conducted in Germany forthe flight.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, we really need to overcome these constraints in order to build a low-altitude economy or industry.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We first need to have a national initiative involving a triple helix of Government, industry and of course, the research institutes and universities.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The current activities that we have right now in Singapore is, of course, ST Engineering.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: My company, NEO Aeronautics, we have a 100-kg payload for sports and recreation, it is designed for the US Federal Aviation Administration market, Part 103.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I think the triple helix forming a consortium of the Government agencies such as CAAS, Economic Development Board, Enterprise Singapore, even the Maritime Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and Singapore Tourism Board, can come in and make it much more comprehensive.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I think the first thing of growing any industry is really to have talents.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We never had design engineers or design aerospace engineers in Singapore, but we have lots of maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) engineers for maintaining aircraft.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: And we are glad that we achieved 10% of the total MRO market in the world – which means we can do it if we put our mind to it.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, for this intellectual capital, we need to have more manpower and talent, and that goes to the universities or the polytechnics.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Currently, there is no specialisation in such low-altitude mobility or advanced air mobility technology in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: SIT does have a degree programme, but it is much more focused on aerospace.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, I think that we should look in detail for a diploma and degree with specialisation, I would not say a pure degree, but a specialisation, and have quite a bit of conversion programmes for existing engineers to convert or technologies to convert to drone technology or eVTOL technology.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The infrastructure capital is really, really the important part here.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: When I talk about infrastructure capital, I am also looking at the regulations.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: CAAS has spearheaded the development of the advanced air mobility technology regulatory standards in Asia Pacific.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: That is trying to harmonise our standards with the rest of the Asia Pacific countries.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I understand that they are also upgrading it, but it is actually for a small payload.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: If we want to go for a bigger payload, I think we really need to have bigger test facility.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, we have progressed, but we really need a turbo boost, with much more resources and aggressive plans.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Testing drones or eVTOL in Singapore is really difficult.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: You can ask for a field, which is like a football field, and then, you try to fly around, and then, the rains come and it is hot and there is no dedicated place for you to have your workshop.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, I suggest that we should identify a location, whether in a university or a research institute, to have at least half a football field with at least 20 metres for flight test and everyone can go there – because I do not think we can afford a lot of such flight test centres.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But we need to think out of the box because that itself allow us to just hover.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, a dedicated sandbox or flight test facility just allows us to hover.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: What is really important is the test flight, and that needs space.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, I think we should think without the box.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: It means if the box is Singapore, we should get out of Singapore, and therefore have a regional sandbox.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: And if you have a regional sandbox, that means our authorities have to work with the authorities in neighbouring countries for joint certification, joint flight test, joint recognition.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I think that will allow us to harmonise our standards and allow us to work with different authorities and facilitate cross border drone flying or eVTOL flights.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: The last part is on the innovation capital.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: In manufacturing, we will not be able to compete based on the manufacturing capacity.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: But we should focus really on what we do best – highly value-added jobs.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: I think that is in applications and also business models.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: For example, we can have purposefully built drones for oil spill disbursement.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: We can do it for our ports and it can be extended to many, many ports in the world.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, that is one application with the right business model.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, you can airlift it out as necessary.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: Give us a completely different way of operating a business.

speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
text: So, moving facilities or bus or trucks or bicycles into the air is not just simply moving into the air.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government pays close attention to the development of the low-altitude economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Indeed, drones and eVTOLs can be viable options for economic, transport and logistics uses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with Dr Neo that these technologies provide opportunities to enhance safety and productivity, enable new operational capabilities and services, and support innovation, across multiple domains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In particular, Dr Neo spoke at length about eVTOLs, which his company, NEO Aeronautics, focuses on, and mentioned air mobility, air tourism and air logistics as areas of opportunity for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, eVTOLs could eventually become a viable option for cross-border travel to adjacent offshore islands, or even cross-border cargo transfer with neighbouring countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to monitor the progress of eVTOL technologies and its safety and cost considerations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In contrast, drone technology is at a more mature stage, with more viable and developed use cases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In Singapore, public sector agencies and commercial players are already using drones in practical, beneficial and meaningful ways across numerous domains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For logistics, we are already trialling the use of drones for ship‑to‑shore deliveries at our port, to transfer and turnaround high-value or essential items.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: By reducing the need for frequent boat trips, drones alleviate manpower demands and minimise risks faced by maritime workers when operating in challenging sea conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For land transport, drones already help to inspect Singapore’s train and road tunnels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They allow our engineers to carry out their inspections more efficiently and with greater precision, while reducing the need for manpower to operate in potentially hazardous or hard-to-access environments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For aviation, commercial firms are exploring the use of drones for visual inspections of aircraft, to complement existing maintenance processes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This allows for faster checks, enhance accuracy and improve safety outcomes, freeing up our maintenance personnel to focus their expertise where it is most needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For the built environment, the Building and Construction Authority, and the Housing and Development Board already use drones to conduct periodic façade inspections in a faster and more efficient manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In October last year, the Ministry of National Development also trialled the use of drones to conduct high-rise ledge cleaning in Punggol, which would otherwise need to be conducted by workers on gondolas, which incurs higher safety risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We hope to scale up such operations so that more buildings in Singapore can be assessed and maintained using drones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For security, the Singapore Police Force deploys drones to monitor crowd numbers in real-time during major events like the National Day Parade or the Marina Bay Countdown.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As you can see, there are many use cases that our various public sector agencies are already using drones for.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government has sought to create a conducive ecosystem in Singapore for the safe experimentation, development and deployment of drones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: First, we support research and innovation through trials, sandboxes and funding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with Dr Neo that these are important for rigorous testing within safe and controlled environments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This helps us determine the viability of new use cases and figure out how drone technologies and operational processes can be further refined to meet desired outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, PUB worked with ST Engineering to use drones to monitor water quality and activities at six reservoirs, which is a faster and more accurate alternative to the traditional method of in-person patrols.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We also identify areas that we can temporarily use as sandboxes for flight trials.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the case of the NTU research team which Dr Neo mentioned, CAAS facilitated the initial hover tests of their prototype eVTOL at the former Turf City racecourse in Kranji last year, ahead of its public unveiling at this year’s Singapore Airshow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will review how we can expand testing sites, including exploring overseas sandboxes in partnership with regional neighbours, as Dr Neo has suggested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These can be located further from urban areas and provide a safer and larger environment to trial larger drones and eVTOLs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, we adapt and streamline our rules regularly to allow a wider scope of low-altitude operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This increased the flexibility and productivity of these inspections, and reduced operating costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also facilitated trials for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These flights can safely operate over larger areas and longer distances away from the drone operator, potentially with reduced manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Ministry of Home Affairs is exploring using beyond-visual-line-of-sight drones to deliver automated external defibrillators during emergencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also revised our regulations to allow commercial operators to seek approval on a per-activity rather than per-drone basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In particular, this has benefited drone light show operators, who handle thousands of drones at a go to create visually stunning spectacles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, we are investing in talent and manpower, as Dr Neo had suggested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are intensifying education efforts to promote the responsible use of drones, develop suitable technical skills and nurture interest in low-altitude technologies for Singaporeans of all backgrounds and ages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are working closely with our educational institutions to integrate drone-related courses into formal curricula.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Neo suggested creating specialisations in advanced air mobility technologies, especially at the tertiary level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Those taking aerospace engineering courses at university can today access an increasing variety of drone-related modules.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Several primary and secondary schools have also introduced drone flying with their curricula or as part of the Applied Learning Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond our educational institutions, there is a wide range of facilities, workshops and courses available to the wider public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the same time, CAAS partners with vendors, such as Just Fly It, to conduct hands-on workshops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members of the public may also use their SkillsFuture credits to attend short-term drone operation courses by institutions, such as the Singapore Management University and Institute of Technical Education, to ensure that their skills are kept up to date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While we have made considerable progress thus far, we know that more can definitely be done.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And this will require overcoming certain constraints, which Dr Neo has alluded to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With multiple airports and air bases, and flights coming and going constantly, the use of our low-altitude airspace will need to be managed carefully between civil and military aircraft, and drones and eVTOLs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Second, Singapore has a dense and highly built-up urban environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And this gives rise to complex issues relating to security, safety and privacy, due to the dense high-rise residential areas and closely co-located security-sensitive locations across our island.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, Singapore’s unpredictable weather and tropical climate pose practical challenges for aviation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is something that we already need to manage carefully for large planes at Changi, let alone smaller and more unstable low-altitude aircraft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It is essential for overall aviation safety that we test new technologies rigorously and work out robust operational processes prior to development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Against this backdrop, we have generally adopted a conservative approach in the past.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: But with drone technology becoming more mature, we can do more.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are studying the approaches in overseas jurisdictions and will adapt what is relevant to Singapore’s operating environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Neo mentioned China as an example, and we agree that there are aspects that Singapore can learn from.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Chinese government has also provided strong support for companies involved in drone development and production in the form of tax reliefs, subsidies and industrial parks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In the US too, there has been significant progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Commercial companies like Wing, a Google spin-off that our Acting Minister of Transport visited just last month, have commenced delivery operations across the country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In these cities, regulatory frameworks are evolving rapidly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For instance, some cities in China have recently tightened their regulations for recreational and civilian drone operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And in the US, the regulatory frameworks vary considerably depending on the state and the city.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In Singapore, the Government, as I have mentioned, will continue to closely monitor the evolution of this space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Neo proposed a national strategy on advanced air mobility and the low-altitude economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: He mentioned a “triple-helix approach” involving the Government, industry and research or educational institutions.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Senior Minister of State Sun, could I kindly request you to wrap up?

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: The time allowed for the proceedings has expired.

text: I adjourn the House pursuant to the Standing Order.
